record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.context_brief: automorphism groups of exotic affine spaces
record.original_question: If X is an exotic C^n, must the action of the algebraic automorphism group Aut(X) on X be non-transitive? Is the analogous non-transitivity statement also true for the full group of analytic automorphisms?

evidence.quote: 2.8. QUESTION. Let X be an exotic Cn. Is it true that the action of the automor-phism group Aut X on X is not transitive ? The same question for the group of analyti c automorphisms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a smooth complex affine algebraic variety $X$ of dimension $n$ that is diffeomorphic (equivalently, homeomorphic) to $\mathbb{C}^n$ but not isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$ as an algebraic variety. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ denote the group of algebraic (biregular) automorphisms of $X$, and let $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X)$ denote the group of holomorphic (analytic) automorphisms of $X$.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$, the natural action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ on $X$ is not transitive.

(b) Prove or disprove the analogous statement for the group $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X)$ of analytic automorphisms: must its action on an exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ fail to be transitive?
artifact.category_tag: exotic affine spaces and automorphism groups
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the non-transitivity question for algebraic or analytic automorphism groups acting on exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$. While there is an extensive literature on flexible/transitive automorphism actions on affine varieties and on constructions of exotic affine spaces, no source found settles this particular question in full generality, so the current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Infinite Transitivity on Affine Varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of infinite transitivity for automorphism groups of affine varieties; discusses flexibility but does not resolve transitivity on exotic C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses transitivity on affine varieties without settling the exotic C^n case.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of affine varieties and their Lie algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey of automorphism groups of affine algebraic varieties and related open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys do not report a resolution of non-transitivity for exotic C^n.
